request.spec:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a fiscal year start month (settings, 1 to 12, 1 unless set, not dated;
SETTING_CHANGED key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>; anything else is refused). A fiscal year is
named FY<yyyy> by the calendar year its first day falls in; show on each period the fiscal year its
from-date falls in. A year entry and a button generate that fiscal year's twelve monthly periods
exactly as the period generator does; show how many were made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the fiscal year start month setting, the fiscal year on each period, and the fiscal-year generate button. The main "fiscal year" test passes, and so does scenario 3. Scenarios 1 and 2 still fail, but both fail on steps that have nothing to do with fiscal years.

**What changed**
- **Setting:** a new `fiscal_start_month` column on the sheet (migration `V81`, 1 unless set, also copied when a sheet is cloned). The settings save only accepts `1`–`12`; anything else, like `13` or `x`, shows `settings-error` and writes nothing. A saved value writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=fiscal-start-month value=<month>` to the audit file. On screen it's `setting-fiscal-start-month` and `setting-fiscal-start-month-current`.
- **Generate a fiscal year:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{id}/periods/generate-fy` checks the year is `yyyy`, turns it into the twelve months starting from the sheet's start month, and hands them to the existing generator steps. So months that are already periods, or overlap one, are skipped and each new period is audited as `PERIOD_ADDED`, exactly as the generator does.
- **Screen:** each period row shows `period-fy` (e.g. `FY2025` for a period from 2025-12-20 when the year starts in April). The year box `period-generate-fy-year` and button `period-generate-fy` sit in the existing generate form and share its `period-generated` count and `period-generate-error`, because a `data-testid` can only appear once on the page.

**The two failing scenarios**
- **Scenario 2:** the spec expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"` (line 753). That's a placeholder that never got filled in; the app correctly shows `<sheetId>-p`. No app can pass that line, and I'm not allowed to edit the spec.
- **Scenario 1:** at line 165 the app refuses a claim dated 2026-02-10, and the spec expects it to go through. I reproduced it directly against the server and got "The period P1 is closed" (409) from the existing closed-period check:
  - Terms of 7 were saved from the sheet's today, 2026-03-20, so a February claim still gets the default 14 days.
  - That puts its due date on 2026-03-02, inside P1, which is closed.
  
  I didn't change any claim or period-closing logic. If the spec is right here, that check needs a separate decision.

Port 3000 was already in use by another process on this machine, so my server couldn't start there and the first run tested something else. I ran `bin/e2e` with `PORT=3017` instead and left the other processes alone.
